g.text: theos: one model, one engine, two runtimes
The same YAML and the same decisions run on a cluster or in a Claude Code session. Only the adapters differ.
the project repository's model/ files: whole theos.factory.io/v1beta1 manifests
Crew · Agent (now read by both runtimes)
no runtime field: the runtime is who reads it
internal/engine: one loop for both runtimes
imports internal/model and internal/ports only, so it can't reach Kubernetes
start a Task · offer a turn
theos drives: its reconcilers start the agents
TaskStore: Task objects and their status
Workers: an Agent Sandbox pod per turn; theos pushes the work
Capabilities: all: fence, model proxy, checkpoints, cost, the operator's merge
Harness: claude-code, headless inside the sandbox
Runs on: a Kubernetes cluster, installed with the Helm chart
a Claude Code session drives: it asks theos what is next
TaskStore: the task/<container>-<issue> branch and its issue's markers
Workers: an offer marker that theos next hands out; the session pulls the work
Capabilities: no sandbox, no scheduler, cost unreported; a person merges
Harness: claude-code, one subagent per Agent the Crew names
Runs on: a laptop, the desktop app, or a Claude Code cloud session
One Task in a Claude Code session
the lead calls theos mcp; theos decides every transition
theos: the Crew tick starts the Task
creates its branch, posts the offer
changes asked: round 2 with the feedback
three levels; anyone can add one without touching the engine
0 any MCP client: the work tools,
one role per session, no code
1 LeadFiles: role files in the tool's
Git host: the only shared state
both runtimes read and write here, so a lead session that goes away loses only what it didn't push
